# Operator Note — Heat Treat Hydraulic Forging Press two

Scope
This note supplements the maintenance manual reference for the heat treat hydraulic forging press two. It is intended for shop operators and maintenance technicians to reinforce safe operation and routine care between scheduled service intervals.

Key checks before startup
Verify work area is clean and free of loose material. Confirm mechanical guards and safety interlocks are engaged. Inspect visible hydraulic lines and fittings for seepage or abrasion. Check indicator panels for normal status and confirm emergency stop functions before placing any load on the press.

During operation
Monitor hydraulic system sound and response; unusual noise or sluggish movement requires immediate shutdown and notification of maintenance. Maintain steady cycle rhythm to avoid thermal or mechanical shock. Keep operator controls and floor area clear of oil and swarf to prevent slips and inadvertent actuation.

Post-shift tasks
Wipe accessible surfaces to remove scale and oil residue. Verify reservoir sight level and filter status visually and log any deviations. Grease guideways and pivot points at manufacturer recommended intervals and record work in the press log. Report worn seals, bent tooling, or misalignment to engineering for corrective action.

Safety and escalation
Always follow lockout/tagout procedures for any intervention. Do not attempt internal hydraulic repairs unless qualified and authorized. For persistent faults, escalate to maintenance supervision and reference the main maintenance manual for detailed diagnostics and parts information.
